items.title: KICK Account Executive
items.description: Are you ready to get the Easygo Edge? Obsessed with live streaming, gaming and the creator economy? Fluent in digital advertising and programmatic buying but want to build something monumental rather than just clock into a traditional, slow moving media network. This is your sandbox. We’re after someone hungry to execute, scale and close revenue generating ad sales opportunities as our global presence takes off. What you’ll build with us: This is a dynamic commercial role for a highly independent operator who thrives in high growth environments, creating their own templates, processes and workflows while getting deals done. Expect to drive net new revenue and manage the campaign lifecycle from pitch through to optimisation, upsells and cross-sells, monetising KICK's explosive global inventory of display, video and branded placements. We know that innovation ignites when we build and create together, in person. This is a full-time opportunity at our Melbourne office. You’ll work right where it all happens, surrounded by our fearless crew shipping high-impact work. Who is Easygo? We’re a high-growth, high-velocity tech company with millions of eyeballs on us every day. We’re building the future of fearless tech. We’re the creators behind some of the most popular brands including Stake, KICK and Easygo Games. While they command a fierce global following, our crew is employed directly by Easygo and that’s where the real fun happens. We’re always looking for people who are hungry, humble and move fast. People who are ready to Unify , Disrupt and Evolve with us. With us you’ll grow faster and go further. Your work has impact. And that gives you an edge you can’t get anywhere else. The impact you’ll make: Ad Sales & Pipeline Management Own the execution of the ad sales cycle: prospecting, qualification, pitching, negotiating, and closing media deals with brands and agencies. Maintain a clean and healthy commercial pipeline within CRM and Order Management tools, ensuring reliable deal tracking and revenue projections. Assist in developing and refining client-facing materials, media kits, and rate cards tailored to the fast-evolving needs of international advertisers. Negotiate insertion orders (IOs), programmatic access (PMPs/PG), and custom brand integrations. Actively contribute to meeting and exceeding group commercial milestones as KICK’s global monetization capability scales. Post-Sales Support & Account Growth Monitor active campaigns to ensure successful execution, tracking client delivery and maximising ROI performance metrics. Act as a dedicated commercial point of contact post-sale, identifying organic paths to secure campaign renewals, cross-sells, and programmatic spend expansions. External Engagement & Cross-functional Delivery Work hand-in-hand with the Creator Partnerships team to monetise international campaign leads, cross-selling ad placements into secondary markets and activating commercial pipeline opportunities brought in by the partnerships ecosystem. Coordinate closely with Ad Operations, Product, and Marketing teams to ensure smooth campaign scheduling, troubleshooting, and commercial alignment. Actively design, establish, and optimise the documentation, sales collateral workflows, and templates required to transition the ad sales desk from startup chaos to a streamlined commercial engine. Your track record: Experience in digital ad sales, media buying, agency sales or commercial digital revenue operations Deep operational comfort with programmatic ecosystems: DSP/SSP mechanics, PMPs, PG and automated audience targeting A proven track record managing an active pipeline and independently driving revenue Operational familiarity with ad sales platforms, CRM workflows and Order Management Systems Solid grounding in digital advertising fundamentals across display, video pre/mid-rolls and native sponsorships A self starter history of executing in ambiguous, unpolished, fast moving startup environments Refined communication, negotiation and presentation skills Bonus points if you also have: Direct experience or familiarity with creator networks, streaming ecosystems, live broadcasting, entertainment or gaming platforms A second language, spoken natively or professionally (Spanish, Portuguese or Arabic), to work closely with international partners Existing commercial connections with international agencies, cross-border programmatic buyers or global digital platforms Here are our benefits and perks: Sharpening your edge The ultimate sandbox. Exciting, on-the-job learning opportunities. 1 in 3 of our people level up their roles every year. If you deliver, you move. items.title: Research & Education Sales Lead, Beneficial Deployments
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team accelerates the work of organizations doing some of the world's most important under-resourced work: nonprofits, education institutions, scientific researchers, and organizations advancing economic mobility. Education institutions sit at the center of that mission. They train the next generation, they produce the science the rest of the world builds on, and they are structurally short on time, budget, and technical capacity to figure out new technology on their own. You will lead our targeted approach to higher education, with a specific focus on research institutes, research intensive universities, and schools focused on access like community colleges and MSIs. You will also support K12 staff and educators across the globe, in particular in low and middle income countries, where teachers and school staff are the users and the district is often the buyer. Where our scaled motion reaches thousands of organizations one to many, this role is the opposite end of the same ecosystem: a deliberately short list of institutions where depth matters, where a lab, a department, or a whole campus adopting Claude changes what science gets done, and where the buying process runs through provosts, research offices, district superintendents, procurement, grant budgets, and security review. Reach comes first, and commercial results follow from it. That ordering is deliberate and it is shared across every leader on this team: a research institute that adopts Claude to move its science faster is a win on its own terms, and you will be measured on creating that value with the institutions that matter most, not only on pipeline. You are the single accountable owner for the research and education Enterprise book globally: its target list, its AEs, its numbers, and its field voice inside Anthropic. You are half seller, half domain translator. You will personally run the most complex institutional deals, and you will be credible in a room of scientists and educators. You know how research is funded, how a university decides, and what it takes for an education sales motion to land in a software company. You will bring that knowledge to the product, applied AI, and marketing teams who build for this audience. This is a player coach seat. You will be directly involved in deals and directing the account executives who cover education today, and the role is expected to grow thoughtfully with more AEs in key regions globally. Key responsibilities scientific discovery and economic access, support for K12 staff and educators Serve as the lead on our most complex institutional deals — setting the pursuit strategy, opening doors with lab and research-office leadership, university provosts, and personally resolving the toughest hurdles: procurement, security review, and grant-funded budgets. Direct and coach the account executives working education accounts today: joint account plans, deal reviews, and a repeatable motion for landing a university and expanding within it. Build the institutional playbook: how an institute goes from a pilot to a working deployment across a department, what good adoption looks like, and when to bring in applied AI, customer success, or partners. Own the book's numbers, institutions reached, activated, and expanded against goals, and use them to decide where the effort goes next. Work in lockstep with our PLG 1:many motion, so that an institution moves cleanly between scaled programs and direct coverage in both directions. Minimum qualifications Education or research sales. You have sold software as a service into universities, research institutes, or academic medical centers, and you have personally closed complex institutional agreements involving procurement, security review, and multiple decision makers. Science or education background. You have trained or worked in a scientific field, or spent a meaningful part of your career selling to or building for scientists or educators, and you can hold a credible conversation with these audiences. Sales leadership. You have led a sales business end to end and been the accountable owner for its results, whether as a team lead, a player coach, or the sole owner of a strategic book. Preferred qualifications Global education landscape: experience selling to universities, research institutes, or school systems in more than one region, an understanding of how funding and procurement differ from country to country, and comfort working across time zones with regional teams. Experience with research funding: grants, indirect costs, and how a fixed annual budget shapes what an institution can buy. Track record landing an institution wide agreement at a research intensive university, and expanding from a single department to a campus or system. Familiarity with how AI is already used in research settings and K12 classrooms, and a point of view on where it should go next. Experience working with academic consortia, national labs, or research networks. An impact, education, research, or mission driven go to market background, and genuine interest in these institutions' constraints. A daily working habit with Claude, and agentic workflows you have built for yourself. You might thrive here if You want your work measured in impact that moves faster and students who get more from their education, not only in pipeline. You have sat in a faculty meeting or a research office and know why the obvious commercial playbook does not work there. You are comfortable being the only person accountable for a book while depending on teams you do not manage. You would rather close the first three institutional deals yourself and write the playbook from what you learned than write the strategy deck first. You find the constraint interesting rather than frustrating: long procurement cycles, grant timelines, and security reviews are the job, not an obstacle to it. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $380,000 — $450,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. The Paid Media Partnerships Lead will represent the Paid Media team in integrated, cross-format opportunities that include events, ambassador deals, and sponsorships with media assets. The role requires close collaboration with the Sponsorship team, country managers, and channel leads to ensure all partnership activity is aligned with brand positioning, performance objectives, and market strategy. We know that innovation ignites when we build and create together, in person. This is a full-time opportunity at our Melbourne office. You’ll work right where it all happens, surrounded by our fearless crew shipping high-impact work. Who is Easygo? We’re a high-growth, high-velocity tech company with millions of eyeballs on us every day. We’re building the future of fearless tech. We’re the creators behind some of the most popular brands including Stake, KICK and Easygo Games. While they command a fierce global following, our crew is employed directly by Easygo and that’s where the real fun happens. We’re always looking for people who are hungry, humble and move fast. People who are ready to Unify , Disrupt and Evolve with us. With us you’ll grow faster and go further. Your work has impact. And that gives you an edge you can’t get anywhere else. The impact you’ll make: Partnership Strategy & Opportunity Identification Proactively identify, evaluate and prioritise digital media partnership opportunities across global and regional markets, balancing always-on investment with event and activation-led deals. Develop and maintain a structured opportunity pipeline, assessing each opportunity against clearly defined criteria across brand positioning, awareness, market authority and acquisition objectives. Build and apply a rigorous partner/publisher assessment framework, defining evaluation criteria tailored to different business objectives and ensuring a consistent, data-informed approach to partnership selection. Maintain visibility of global opportunities (relevant to .com) alongside the ability to identify cross-market efficiencies, for example, a single partnership that spans all LatAm markets rather than negotiating each individually. Negotiation & Commercial Management Lead the negotiation of partnership agreements including commercial terms, media commitments, exclusivity arrangements, deliverable guarantees, and renewal conditions. Drive commercial rigour across the portfolio, ensuring Easygo consistently achieves favourable terms and measurable returns on all partnership investment. Oversee the investment budget in collaboration with regional leads, allocating spend across the portfolio in line with strategic priorities and performance outcomes. Direct Publisher Relationships Own and develop Easygo's direct publisher relationships, building a preferred partner network of premium media owners across key markets and categories. Lead the negotiation and management of direct inventory deals, including tenancy packages, sponsorship integrations, content partnerships and bespoke placement arrangements. Work in close collaboration with the Programmatic Lead to identify where SSP relationships and Private Marketplace (PMP) deals can complement or replace direct arrangements - bringing a commercial and strategic lens to inventory decisions while the Programmatic Lead owns technical execution. Collaborate with the Programmatic Lead on the development of PMPs for both always-on activity and short-term event-led activations (e.g. World Cup, major sporting events) - owning the commercial negotiation and deal structure while the Programmatic Lead governs technical setup and delivery. Balance global ambition with local relevance, ensuring partnership strategy serves both brand-building at scale and acquisition in specific regulated markets. Build a high-performing, commercially minded team capable of managing a complex, multi-market partnership portfolio across brand and performance objectives. Contribute to hiring decisions as the team scales, and develop a team structure that reflects the breadth and ambition of the partnerships function. Collaborate with channel leads across Paid Search, Paid Social and Programmatic to ensure a cohesive, non-duplicative messaging strategy across all paid touchpoints. Contribute to integrated planning cycles - providing partnership forecasts, inventory insights, and activation plans to inform broader media and marketing strategy. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more - deeply embedded where people get things done. You’ll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is seeking a Partner Sales Manager to build and manage strategic partners to expand Glean’s customer reach in the West Region. This individual will be closely aligned to multiple sales segment teams and be responsible for building and executing the partner strategy to drive meaningful revenue impact—in a hands-on, results-oriented role. Build repeatable plays for sourcing new opportunities, including campaigns, events, account mapping, and outbound motions, and maintain clear visibility into partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline. Work cross-functionally with Sales, SE, Marketing, Operations, and Legal to simplify and scale partner processes such as deal registration, approvals, contracts, MDF and reporting. Embed with the sales organization by aligning partners to territories, participating in key deal reviews and account planning, and ensuring partners feel like an extension of the Glean field teams. About you: Outcome- and revenue-oriented partner leader who thinks like a GM/business owner, not just a relationship manager, and is comfortable being accountable for partner-driven pipeline and bookings. Proven experience in channel, alliances, partner management, or business development roles in B2B SaaS. Demonstrated success recruiting, activating, and growing SI/VAR or similar partners, not just managing inherited relationships. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Partner Account Manager for Japan, you will be responsible for building, managing, and scaling strategic partnerships with both System Integrators (SIs) and resellers to accelerate the adoption of our solutions in the Japanese enterprise market. You will work at the intersection of cutting-edge technology and Japan's unique business ecosystem, helping partners integrate our products into their solution portfolios and joint go-to-market strategies. As a Partner Account Manager, you will focus on growing reseller business in Japan and achieving quarterly revenue targets through new customers and upsells. The position involves direct collaboration with partners and internal teams to overcome obstacles and implement growth strategies. Responsibilities include designing partner recruitment, enablement, and go-to-market plans, using a test-and-learn approach in ambiguous situations. Strong business creation skills are needed to identify joint value propositions and explore co-selling models. While revenue contribution is the key metric, building scalable partner engagement and executing joint initiatives are crucial for consistent growth. This role is critical to establishing and expanding our presence in Japan through the partner ecosystem, enabling us to serve Japanese enterprises at scale. You will be instrumental in building our channel strategy from the ground up in one of the world's most sophisticated technology markets. growth and revenue targets Build and maintain executive-level relationships within Japanese partner organizations, navigating complex organizational structures and decision-making processes Own the full partner lifecycle from initial engagement through long-term strategic alignment, including regular business reviews and QBRs Plan and deliver partner-facing activities, such as training sessions, email campaigns, webinars, and joint events Negotiate and structure partnership agreements including technical integration terms, resale agreements, and revenue-sharing models Business Development & qualify, and close enterprise opportunities in key verticals (manufacturing, financial services, retail, telecommunications, life sciences) Drive joint sales activities including customer workshops, seminars, proof-of-concepts, and strategic account planning Track pipeline development, forecast revenue, and report on partnership performance metrics with detailed accuracy Manage channel conflict and ensure healthy ecosystem dynamics between direct sales, SI partners, and resellers Enablement & Solution Development Lead comprehensive enablement programs including technical training, certification development, and sales methodology alignment Work closely with partner practices to develop joint solutions and industry-specific offerings tailored to Japanese market requirements documentation, and partner portals Facilitate knowledge transfer between Anthropic and Japanese partner technical teams Go-to-Market Leadership Design and execute joint marketing campaigns Develop customer success stories and case studies that resonate with Japanese enterprise buyers Partner with internal teams to localize global GTM strategies for the Japanese market Represent the company at items.title: Channel Partner Manager
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role As a Channel Partner Manager for Korea, you will be responsible for building, managing, and scaling strategic partnerships with both System Integrators (SIs) and resellers to accelerate the adoption of our solutions in the Korean market. You will work at the intersection of cutting-edge technology and Korea's unique business ecosystem, helping partners integrate our products into their solution portfolios and joint go-to-market strategies. As a Channel Partner Manager, you will focus on growing the partner Anthropic reseller and services business in Korea and achieving quarterly revenue and partner attach targets through new customers and upsells. You'll be the local owner of these partner relationships in Korea. Our partners will look to you for everything that makes the channel work day to day from initial onboarding to deal registration, enablement, billing and contracting questions, escalations. Our internal teams will look to you for what is happening in the market, how partners are driving new opportunities and growth within existing customers. You'll work closely with the local sales team and the central program team, co-selling on partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities and managing direct versus partner conflict as deals arise. Strong business creation skills are needed to identify joint value propositions and explore co-selling models. Much of the process for running the channel in Korea doesn't exist yet, and building it will be a large part of the job in the first year. While revenue contribution is the key metric, building scalable partner engagement and executing joint initiatives are crucial for consistent growth. This is an early role in a new market for a program we expect to grow well beyond its first two countries. The habits you establish with our first partners in Korea will shape how the program works everywhere else. Key responsibilities Own the day-to-day relationships with Anthropic's strategic resellers and system integrators in Korea, acting as their primary local point of contact, including billing, contracting and general queries Own deal registration and pipeline discipline with partners, making sure registrations are submitted and validated, conflicts are cleared, and named end-customer reporting is complete on every deal Forecast and report partner pipeline and performance against the quarterly revenue and partner attach targets, and own the Korea channel number with the central program team Negotiate resale agreements and commercial terms with partners alongside the central program team and Legal Co-sell with the local account team on partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities, and manage direct versus partner conflict as deals arise Develop and execute business plans with System Integrators and strategic resellers to drive mutual growth and revenue targets Build and maintain executive-level relationships within Korean partner organizations, navigating complex organizational structures and decision-making processes Support partner onboarding end to end, from diligence and agreement execution through readiness ahead of launch, including for partners who join the program after launch Coordinate partner certification and enablement with the central enablement lead, including Korean-language delivery and ongoing recertification Manage Anthropic's counterpart relationships with the cloud hyperscalers AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure in Korea, including the Marketplace private offer motion that reseller deals run through Work with the central program team on program governance, margin mechanics, and escalations, and build the local processes and working rhythms the channel needs where none exist yet, feeding what you learn from partners back to the program team Run regular business reviews and QBRs with each partner against the joint plan Own partner co-marketing in Korea, agreeing a joint marketing plan with each partner and Channel Marketing, funding it through MDF where it qualifies, and delivering the announcements, campaigns, webinars and events that turn the partnership into pipeline Minimum qualifications Experience managing channel or reseller partner relationships in enterprise software or cloud Experience working with large Korean systems integrators or cloud managed service providers, and an understanding of how partner-led selling works in Korean enterprise, public sector, and financial services accounts Working knowledge of channel program mechanics such as deal registration and partner tiering Full professional fluency in Korean and professional working proficiency in English, written and spoken, including the ability to deliver enablement to partners in Korean Comfort joining a new program early: hands-on, structured, and able to build process where none exists yet Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial Preferred qualifications Experience with cloud marketplace resale, particularly AWS Marketplace private offers, or with AWS partner teams more generally Familiarity with margin and rebate mechanics in a partner program Experience bringing existing, informal partner activity into a structured program, or joining a partner program at or before launch Experience on the systems integrator or managed service provider side of a vendor relationship, as well as the vendor side Familiarity with how enterprises and public sector organizations in Korea are evaluating and adopting AI Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: Work with the Best Orderly Network is a combination of an orderbook-based trading infrastructure and a robust liquidity layer offering spot and perpetual futures orderbooks. Unlike traditional platforms, Orderly doesn’t have a front end; instead, it operates at the core of the ecosystem, providing essential services to projects built on top of it. Our DEX white-label solution is carefully crafted to save builders time and capital while granting access to our bootstrapped liquidity. Picture having the best features of CEXs while keeping settlements on-chain and maintaining full self-custody. With Orderly, anyone can create a trading application thanks to our seamless plug-and-play experience leveraging our liquidity and composability. Looking ahead, our grand vision is to create an omnichain protocol, connecting traders from both EVM and non-EVM chains within the same orderbook. A Glimpse into Your Future at Orderly Network Orderly's Partnership team accelerates the growth of our ecosystem by identifying, engaging, and supporting builders and partners who build on top of Orderly's infrastructure. In this role, you will be the driving force behind expanding our partner ecosystem — building and managing a robust pipeline of prospective partners, tracking relationship progress through structured CRM workflows, and ensuring partners are activated and growing on Orderly. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who thinks in systems — who can apply internet-era frameworks (funnel management, data-driven tracking, automated workflows) to relationship building and pipeline management at scale. What will you be working on? Build and maintain a structured pipeline of prospective partners across multiple verticals (DeFi, gaming, NFT, infrastructure, and beyond), using CRM tools and data-driven tracking systems to manage the full lifecycle from prospect to activation Apply internet-thinking frameworks to relationship management — treat partner outreach as a funnel: identify → qualify → engage → activate → grow, with clear metrics and tracking at each stage Develop and execute new growth initiatives to expand the Orderly ecosystem Collaborate with BD, DevRel, Marketing, and Operations teams to implement ecosystem growth initiatives end-to-end Engage with builders, investors, exchanges, and infrastructure providers to drive ecosystem growth and partnership activation Manage grants programs and hackathon participation to attract builders to build on Orderly and encourage composability Research emerging protocols and verticals; collaborate with L1/L2 ecosystems to drive token utility and cross-chain adoption Maintain a clean, up-to-date partner database with clear status tracking, next-step actions, and follow-up cadences Who will you be working with? Maintain close collaboration with Marketing, Operations, Product & BD Teams. About you Bilingual fluency in English and Mandarin Chinese — you can switch seamlessly between both languages in business settings (native-level English speaker, e.g., ABC or equivalent bilingual profile, strongly preferred) Energetic and early-career — you're young, hungry, and eager to prove yourself; we value drive and adaptability over years of tenure Internet-native mindset — you naturally think in terms of funnels, pipelines, tracking systems, and data-driven relationship management; you're comfortable using CRM tools, spreadsheets, and automation to manage large volumes of relationships without losing personal touch 2+ years of experience in ecosystem growth, BD, partnerships, or portfolio support at a blockchain (L1/L2), venture firm, or internet/tech company — with demonstrated experience onboarding and growing projects from the ground up You are biased toward action while respecting team-oriented priorities You are no-ego, adaptable, entrepreneurial, detail-oriented You are an excellent speaker and writer You are personable and able to manage expectations across many stakeholders and multiple on-going relationships Interested in Learning More? Our hiring process begins by meeting with our People Team, who help facilitate the process of placing you in your new role. You can expect to share your experience and ideas in online video interviews with our hiring team, made up of management and potential new colleagues. If you have experience in developing trading systems or financial-related products is a plus. You can prepare for this interview by mentally organizing your strategies and opinions on topics such as Web3, cryptocurrency trading platforms, and your vision of how to succeed. Share this! Don’t be afraid of friends or co-workers stealing this job! If you are amazing and smart we will find a place for you. Check out our External Referral Incentives Program as well.

items.title: National Security Partnerships Lead, Intelligence and International Security
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are hiring a National Security Partnerships Lead to grow and manage our relationships with the U.S. Intelligence Community and with allied intelligence and security services. You will report to the Head of National Security Policy and advise company leadership on intelligence and allied-partner matters. You will help partner security organizations build policies that let them adopt frontier AI quickly and for high-impact missions, while deploying it safely and avoiding incidents. You will also engage U.S. and foreign government officials on the policy frameworks that guide the international distribution and deployment of Anthropic's models. You will own a portfolio of government partnerships end to end: setting the agenda with senior counterparts, structuring the agreements and channels that govern each relationship, and bringing partner requirements and concerns back into Anthropic's policy, product, research, and safeguards decisions. You will work closely with our public sector sales, legal, security, and threat intelligence teams. Key responsibilities Lead Anthropic's strategic engagement with U.S. Intelligence Community elements and allied intelligence and security services. Help partner security organizations develop the policies and governance that enable rapid, high-impact adoption of frontier AI and safe deployments that avoid incidents. Identify high-leverage national security deployments with partners, and support our public sector sales team in delivering them. Brief senior government security officials in the U.S. and allied capitals on frontier AI capabilities, risks, and Anthropic's approach to safety. Engage U.S. and foreign government officials on the national security implications of the international distribution and deployment of Anthropic's models, and advise company leadership on partner equities in those decisions. Partner with federal affairs, international policy, communications, and marketing on national security matters, including engagement with the Executive Branch and Congress. Travel regularly within the U.S. and to allied countries. Minimum qualifications Substantial experience in national security, including work in or with the Intelligence Community. Direct experience managing relationships with foreign partner governments or services. An active TS/SCI clearance, or one held within the last two years, and the ability to obtain and maintain it. Experience negotiating formal agreements or partnerships between governments, or between government and industry. A working understanding of how intelligence organizations operate, including classification, liaison relationships, and how they adopt new technology, and the ability to get things done within those constraints. The ability to brief senior policymakers and officials clearly, and to explain technical subjects without overstating them. Experience working effectively with cross-functional teams, including technical, sales, policy, trust and safety, legal, security, product, research, and communications. Demonstrated interest and experience in a complex technical subject, ideally AI, though defense technology, cybersecurity, or similar fields also count. The ability to build structure where little exists and to manage competing priorities without waiting for perfect clarity. Preferred qualifications 10+ years of experience in national security, including substantial work in or with the Intelligence Community. Experience in a liaison, foreign partnership, or foreign disclosure role. Experience in related private-sector roles, such as at technology, cybersecurity, or defense companies. Regional expertise or language skills relevant to allied partners. Hands-on familiarity with large language models and how they can be misused. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $295,000 — $345,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: Are you ready to get the Easygo Edge? We're looking for an Affiliate Coordinator to join our Marketing team and expand our brand's reach and revenue by managing a portfolio of performance driven affiliate partners. Think SEO, PPC, media buying and mobile apps. The role suits someone commercially minded, comfortable with numbers and confident dealing directly with partners. What you’ll build with us: Reporting to our Senior Affiliate Manager, this role sits at the centre of our affiliate program. The partners you look after drive high quality traffic through diverse digital channels, and your job is to make each partnership work harder for customer acquisition. It takes a sharp analytical mindset and the ability to adapt as the digital landscape evolves. Salary: $80,000-90,000 We know that innovation ignites when we build and create together, in person. This is a full-time opportunity at our Melbourne office. You’ll work right where it all happens, surrounded by our fearless crew shipping high-impact work. Who is Easygo? We’re a high-growth, high-velocity tech company with millions of eyeballs on us every day. We’re building the future of fearless tech. We’re the creators behind some of the most popular brands including Stake, KICK and Easygo Games. While they command a fierce global following, our crew is employed directly by Easygo and that’s where the real fun happens. We’re always looking for people who are hungry, humble and move fast. People who are ready to Unify , Disrupt and Evolve with us. With us you’ll grow faster and go further. Your work has impact. And that gives you an edge you can’t get anywhere else. The impact you’ll make: Identify, research and onboard new affiliates to expand our network across a range of traffic sources Benchmark our program, commission structures and partner portfolio against key competitors through in depth competitive analysis Stay ahead of trends in SEO, paid media and app marketing, plus shifts in search engine and AI algorithms Act as the main point of contact for your affiliates, owning their ongoing engagement and support Negotiate improved deal and commission structures to maximise profitability and traffic volume Analyse performance data to optimise existing deals, spot growth opportunities and keep traffic quality aligned with business goals Monitor KPIs and report on program performance Protect brand integrity by vetting partners, monitoring their activity and ensuring program compliance Keep everything running smoothly by managing admin tasks and coordinating with cross functional teams to resolve issues and streamline processes Your track record: At least 1 year of proven experience in performance based affiliate marketing or a similar data driven digital marketing role Strong analytical skills and keen attention to detail, with demonstrated proficiency in Google Sheets or Excel for analysis, forecasting and reporting Experience with affiliate or SEO tools such as Ahrefs, Semrush or similar to run competitive analysis and uncover new opportunities Excellent negotiation and relationship management skills to secure mutually beneficial agreements with performance driven partners Strong verbal and written communication for clear, professional interaction with internal teams and external affiliates A proactive, problem solving mindset, able to troubleshoot quickly and propose data backed solutions Highly organised and self motivated Bonus points if you also have: Knowledge of performance marketing channels, including how search engine algorithms and AI impact traffic acquisition An understanding of streaming platforms for content creators Familiarity with the sports betting, online gambling or crypto industries A strong ability to learn and adapt, keeping pace with new tools, automation and shifts in the digital landscape Here are our benefits and perks: Sharpening your edge The ultimate sandbox. Exciting, on-the-job learning opportunities. 1 in 3 of our people level up their roles every year. If you deliver, you move. Competitive pay and bonus scheme Market-synced pay that respects your craft and location. Performance-based bonus recognition based on your impact (up to 20%). Help us build our crew and get paid for it with our high-value referral bonus. Because great people know great people. Other perks 18 weeks paid parental leave for primary carers Smooth Parental Return: Ease back into work with 12 weeks of transition support, including fully paid Fridays off during your first three months back Access to Employee Assistance Program Wednesday massages In-house baristas serve you free coffee, fresh juices and smoothies. Daily catered breakfast and regular company-wide events. Snack walls and drink fridges on every floor. Fun, modern office spaces. Pool tables, table tennis, gaming consoles and an F1 simulator. We play fair. We hire fair. True to our value of ‘Play fair’ we always hire fair. Our work and our brands are fuelled by our diverse culture. We hire for talent and grit. But we never discriminate. Your race, religion, nationality, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, marital, veteran, or disability status won’t affect our hiring decision, or your trajectory here. Come as you are and get the Easygo edge.

items.title: Private Equity Partnerships Manager
items.description: About Glean: Glean is the Work AI platform that helps everyone work smarter with AI. What began as the industry’s most advanced enterprise search has evolved into a full-scale Work AI ecosystem, powering intelligent Search, an AI Assistant, and scalable AI agents on one secure, open platform. With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles. At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level. Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. With customers across 50+ industries and 1,000+ employees in more than 25 countries, we’re helping the world’s largest organizations make every employee AI-fluent, and turning the superintelligent enterprise from concept into reality. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more - deeply embedded where people get things done. You’ll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company. About the Role: Glean is seeking a Private Equity Partnerships Manager to build and scale our ecosystem with leading private equity and investment firms. In this role, you will own relationships with top sponsors and drive adoption of Glean across their portfolios, sitting at the intersection of PE, AI, and enterprise transformation. You’ll structure and manage portfolio‑wide commercial frameworks, oversee deployment motions across PortCos, and ensure Glean delivers measurable EBITDA and enterprise value impact for PE‑backed businesses. This is a manager‑level, quota‑carrying role within Partnerships, working closely with Sales, Marketing, Product, and Customer Success. You are fluent in PE economics, comfortable navigating multi‑stakeholder environments across funds and PortCos, and able to manage AI value‑creation plays from term sheet through exit. Success is measured by converting PE partnerships into live deployments, pipeline, and revenue across your sponsors. You will: Drive PE partnership strategy & deal management Structure, negotiate, and execute PE partnership agreements (preferred pricing, portfolio‑wide frameworks, lighthouse PortCo plays). Draft reusable cross‑portfolio pricing and partnership agreements with Legal, Finance, and RevOps. Coordinate internal approvals and external sign‑off with GP leadership, operating partners, and PortCo executives. Maintain standardized pricing and commercial constructs so AEs have clear guidance on using PE frameworks in deals. Sponsor relationship management Serve as Glean’s primary day‑to‑day contact for multiple PE sponsors. Build deep relationships with operating partners, portfolio ops, deal teams, and technology/data leaders. Run recurring cadences (QBRs, portfolio and pipeline reviews, exec check‑ins) to surface and advance opportunities. Maintain current views of key contacts, portfolios, and in‑flight initiatives per sponsor. Portfolio activation & deployment oversight Drive PortCo activation by identifying high‑value AI use cases (e.g., GTM, finance, engineering, support/back‑office). Support scoping and oversee evaluation, pilot, and rollout cycles with AEs, AI Outcomes/CS, Solutions, and SIs. Coordinate with Product, Engineering, and partners to meet quality, security, and timeline expectations. Track and communicate deployment metrics (adoption, usage, revenue/cost/EBITDA impact) to sponsors and management teams. Revenue, pipeline & program performance Own pipeline development and revenue targets for assigned sponsors. Maintain a rolling forecast of opportunities across portfolios (sourced and influenced). Work with AEs to map portfolios, track activity, and prioritize accounts by sponsor focus, AI readiness, and value potential. Ensure clean partner/opportunity data in CRM and build dashboards for PE‑sourced/influenced pipeline, ARR, coverage, and velocity. Surface insights and recommendations to improve motions, offers, and enablement. Enablement & cross‑functional coordination Build and update concise enablement assets (one‑pagers, decks, FAQs, playbooks) for sponsors and PortCos. Develop case studies and portfolio‑level proof points; run enablement sessions and workshops to drive adoption. Design and execute programmatic engagement (fireside chats, webinars, roundtables, dinners) with PE and PortCo execs. Partner with Sales and Enablement on portfolio‑wide sessions and briefings. Collaborate with Sales, Marketing, Product, Legal, Security, RevOps, and Customer Success to move deals forward and feed learnings into the roadmap. Coordinate with SI / implementation partners on joint delivery, ensuring aligned messaging and execution. About you: Experience 5–10+ years in enterprise SaaS and/or fintech across partnerships, BD, sales, PE‑backed operating roles, or management consulting serving PE clients. Direct experience with technology partnerships with PE sponsors or multi‑entity / portfolio structures strongly preferred. Proven track record working with sales to drive pipeline and revenue (co‑sell, partner‑sourced deals, complex accounts). Strong program/project management skills: multiple concurrent workstreams, stakeholders, and deadlines with high attention to detail. Able to operate as both strategist and executor across cross‑portfolio deployments. PE & commercial acumen Strong familiarity with fund structures, GP/carry economics, value‑creation playbooks, and sponsor–PortCo dynamics. Comfortable with commercial discussions (pricing, discounts, basic economics) and iterating on term sheets within guardrails. AI & technical fluency Fluent in AI and agentic AI concepts; can credibly discuss Glean with technical teams and PE investors. Able to translate AI capabilities into portfolio‑level value creation narratives (EBITDA, efficiency, growth, multiple expansion). Communication & collaboration Excellent written and verbal communication; comfortable with C‑suite‑level decks and crisp internal updates. Proven ability to build trust and alignment across internal and external stakeholders in fast‑moving environments. Mindset Scrappy, curious, and excited to help define and scale Glean’s PE partnership motion. Thrive in ambiguity and shifting priorities. Passionate about AI’s potential to transform the economy and aligned with Glean’s mission to deliver safe, enterprise‑grade AI with real business impact. Location: This role is hybrid (4 days a week in our New York City office) Compensation & Benefits: The standard OTE (on‑target earnings) range for this position is $250,000 – $300,000 annually, with competitive equity and benefits. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including competitive compensation, Medical, Vision, and Dental coverage, generous time-off policy, and the opportunity to contribute to your 401k plan to support your long-term goals. When you join, you'll receive a home office improvement stipend, as well as an annual education and wellness stipends to support your growth and wellbeing. We foster a vibrant company culture through regular events, and provide healthy lunches daily to keep you fueled and focused. We are a diverse bunch of people and we want to continue to attract and retain a diverse range of people into our organization. We're committed to an inclusive and diverse company. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, civil or family status, age, disability, or race. #LI-HYBRID AI-First Mindset at Glean: At Glean, AI fluency is core to how we work and we're committed to ensuring every new hire feels confident integrating AI into their everyday work. As part of the interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about, design, and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today — prior Glean experience isn't required. Global Data Privacy Notice for Job Candidates and Applicants: Depending on your location, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), or other privacy laws may regulate the way we manage the data of job applicants. Our full notice outlining how data will be processed as part of the application procedure for applicable locations is available in our Privacy Policy . By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. US applicants and their applications are subject to arbitration of disputes as outlined in our Applicant Arbitration Agreement . By clicking “Submit Application,” I confirm that I have read the Global Data Privacy Notice and the Applicant Arbitration Agreement , and I agree to the terms.

items.title: Senior Account Executive - Montreal/Atlantic Canada
items.description: Who are we? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Why this role? In this role, you will have ownership of the full sales cycle - from identifying leads to closing deals with Global 2000, large enterprises within Eastern Canada. We’re looking for an approachable and compelling communicator who loves working with prospects to uncover their needs and feels comfortable developing tailored value propositions around how Cohere’s platform can help them achieve their business goals. You’ll lay the foundation for Cohere’s growth by owning your territory and collaborating with teammates across customer success, sales development, marketing, and solution architecture. You’ll be the voice of the field and help our product and engineering teams prioritize the Cohere roadmap with customer-centric care. It’s a highly self-directed role, so you should be someone who thrives in an unstructured and quickly evolving environment. And your opportunity for impact will be astronomical — Cohere has skies-the-limit potential, and you’ll help us reach it. As an Account Executive you will: - Focus on net-new logo acquisition via outbound activity and relationship building with key stakeholders while also bringing a strong network of key decision-maker and influencer contacts to drive strategic partnerships and win sales opportunities - Work closely with customers and prospects as a consultative, trusted advisor who deeply understands their challenges and goals, their technology ecosystem, and will tailor solutions to drive measurable impact for their businesses - Work in close partnership with channel partners to find opportunities to scale outreach and customer satisfaction in your region - Collaborate with product and engineering teams as well as customer success on strategic motions to deliver solutions to large enterprise customers - Collaborate with Sales Development Representatives to drive top of funnel activity - Own the full sales cycle – from initial outreach through proof-of-concept, deal close, and deployment ; this is not a transactional sale that you can walk away from after the contract is signed but rather requires ongoing oversight of the project to ensure success You may be a good fit if you have: - 8-12+ years of previous B2B sales experience with Global 2000 and large enterprises negotiating and closing transformational multi-year (2-5 year) SaaS deals in the 7 figure range, and a track record of high performance and exceeding quota - Previous experience as a technical consultative salesperson, selling complex products, such as developer tools, API products, or AI / NLP solutions, are a plus. - Previous experience working with customers during the deployment phase of the engagement, aligning on how best to configure and customize the solution that supports success in production and builds trust to set up for expansion and growth - Previous experience working with channel partners such as cloud hyperscalers and system integrators to drive sales cycles and hit shared revenue goals - High tolerance for ambiguity - as an early sales hire, you’ll have to be a self-starter, doer and a strategist who is capable of wearing many hats and doing what it takes to figure out a path to success - Curiosity - you want to go deep on NLP and become an expert on our technology while considering how to fit into a large organization’s technology landscape - Fantastic communication skills - you are a great listener, have a knack for understanding what matters most to others, build strong relationships, can speak to the c-suite, and feel comfortable speaking to both technical and non-technical audiences Additional Requirements: - Deep understanding of the enterprise landscape, including key trends, challenges, and opportunities - Ability to articulate the value of AI and NLP solutions in the context of Fortune 2000 operations. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

items.title: Integrity Sales & Partnerships Lead
items.description: We’re the world’s leading sports technology company, at the intersection between sports, media, and betting. More than 1,700 sports federations, media outlets, betting operators, and consumer platforms across 120 countries rely on our know-how and technology to boost their business. Integrity Sales & Partnerships Lead reports to the VP, Integrity Services and serves as a member of the Integrity Services global Sales & Partnerships team. The role combines business development, strategic account management, commercial planning, and regional sales operations responsibilities to drive sustainable revenue growth across the Integrity Services portfolio. The successful candidate will be responsible for identifying and converting new business opportunities, expanding strategic client relationships, and supporting the execution of the global product-led commercial strategy. Working closely with product owners, operational teams, and other Sportradar business units, the individual will act as a trusted advisor to sporting organisations while contributing directly to regional and global revenue objectives. This position requires a commercially minded and results-oriented professional with strong business acumen, excellent stakeholder management skills, and the ability to balance independent ownership of opportunities with collaborative execution across a global team. THE CHALLENGE Act as a member of the global commercial team, driving new business acquisition, account expansion, and cross-sell opportunities across the full Integrity Services portfolio, including Anti-Match-Fixing, Integrity Education, Due Diligence, Athlete Protection, Anti-Doping, and other Integrity Services solutions. Identify, evaluate, and advance commercial opportunities across sporting entities, including international federations, national federations, leagues, clubs, event organisers, regulators, and other key stakeholders. Own individual revenue, pipeline, and business development targets, contributing directly to regional and global Integrity Services growth objectives. Develop and execute strategic account plans for priority clients, identifying opportunities for contract renewals, service expansion, and long-term partnership growth. Provide exceptional account management and customer care, building trusted relationships with key stakeholders and decision-makers across the sports ecosystem. Collaborate closely with global product owners and commercial colleagues to identify, develop, and progress opportunities across the Integrity Services portfolio. Actively contribute market intelligence, client feedback, and competitive insights to support product development, commercial strategy, and go-to-market planning. Represent Sportradar Integrity Services at industry conferences, forums, workshops, and stakeholder events. Work closely with other Sportradar business units to identify joint opportunities, support strategic pursuits, and maximise the value of existing client relationships. Maintain accurate pipeline, opportunity, contract, and forecasting data within Salesforce, ensuring transparency and consistency across the sales cycle. Support commercial planning and regional forecasting through the preparation of revenue reports, pipeline analysis, business reviews, and market assessments. Contribute to the development of regional market intelligence, identifying emerging trends, governance developments, regulatory changes, competitive dynamics, and growth opportunities. Develop and maintain expert knowledge of the Integrity Services portfolio, products, and market positioning, acting as a trusted internal and external subject matter expert. Drive operational excellence and regional efficiency through disciplined Salesforce utilisation, commercial reporting, pricing consistency, and contract management processes. ABOUT YOU Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Sports Management, International Relations, Law, Finance, Marketing, or a related field. Minimum 5 years of experience in sports business, sports technology, integrity, governance, betting, consulting, or a related commercial environment. Demonstrated success in business development, account management, partnership management, and revenue generation. Strong understanding of the sports ecosystem, including sporting federations, leagues, clubs, governing bodies, regulators, and commercial stakeholders. Proven ability to develop senior stakeholder relationships and navigate complex sales environments. Experience working in an international business environment, collaborating effectively across functions, regions, and product teams. Strong commercial acumen with experience managing sales pipelines, forecasting, and commercial reporting. items.title: Senior Vendor Manager - SMB Sales
items.description: About the Team The SMB Sales team is focused on scaling efficient, high-quality sales execution across a range of commercial motions, including Inbound, Outbound, API Sales, Channel, and SDR. We partner closely with Sales Leadership, Revenue Operations, Finance, Enablement, Program Management, and external vendor partners to build scalable operating models that support growth while maintaining a high bar for performance and customer experience. About the Role As a Senior Vendor Manager, SMB Sales, you will own performance across our outsourced SMB Sales vendor network. This is not a traditional vendor management role. We’re looking for a performance-focused operator who can drive large-scale sales execution through vendor partners, rather than someone primarily focused on vendor relationship management. You will own regional and site-level performance across Tier 1 partners, with responsibility for sales performance, quality, forecasting, governance, operational readiness, and vendor leadership accountability across multiple sales motions. You’ll work at the intersection of Sales Leadership, Revenue Operations, Finance, Enablement, Program Management, and external vendor executives. You will help ensure the machine performs: surfacing issues early, creating accountability, and driving the operating rigor needed to deliver consistently strong outcomes at scale. In this role, you will: - Own regional and site-level performance across revenue, pipeline, conversion, productivity, quality, and other key sales metrics. - Inspect sales funnel health and diagnose whether performance gaps are driven by quality, execution, routing, enablement, staffing, or process issues. - Surface underperformance early, diagnose the underlying drivers, and drive urgency around corrective action. - Build clear corrective action plans with vendor leadership, establish measurable outcomes, and ensure strong follow-through. - Lead Weekly Business Reviews, Monthly Business Reviews, and Quarterly Business Reviews with vendor partners, ensuring governance forums drive decisions, not just reporting. - Build and maintain scorecards that make sales performance, quality, operational health, and risk visible. - Hold vendor leadership accountable for frontline management quality, coaching effectiveness, staffing discipline, and execution rigor. - Own regional adoption of global playbooks, QA frameworks, and operating standards, using quality trends, call reviews, calibration outputs, and conversion analysis to identify opportunities for improvement. - Identify recurring operational failure modes and partner cross-functionally to solve systemic issues while maintaining a high bar for customer experience. - Own forecast quality, pipeline discipline, and risk inspection across assigned regions, building a consistent inspection cadence across motions and partners and pressure-testing vendor forecasts against activity, pipeline, and expected outcomes. - Translate complex operational and performance signals into clear business narratives and recommendations for senior leadership. - Monitor new-hire ramp, certification outcomes, productivity curves, and overall vendor readiness before launching new motions, regions, or major process changes. - Partner with Enablement, Revenue Operations, and Program Management to close readiness gaps and manage capacity against forecasted demand and business priorities. - Help redefine vendor operations for an AI-native sales environment, using automation, AI-enabled workflows, and scalable operating systems to improve seller productivity, forecasting accuracy, quality inspection, execution speed, decision-making, and performance visibility. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have 8+ years of experience in vendor management, sales operations, scaled sales execution, vendor leadership, or commercial operations. - Have direct experience managing outsourced sales or revenue-generating vendor operations. - Have experience working in software, SaaS, cloud, or other high-velocity commercial environments. - Have strong experience working with Tier 1 vendor partners. - Have proven experience owning sales performance across multiple teams, sites, regions, or vendors. - Have a strong understanding of sales funnel metrics, forecasting, conversion, productivity, quality, and operational governance. - Have experience building and running WBRs, QBRs, performance scorecards, and corrective action plans. - Bring strong executive presence and the ability to influence senior internal and external stakeholders.
